featherdrop's server is now a single static **Go binary** — same app, same
zero-knowledge guarantees, same features, but a tiny image with no Node runtime.
This is a **drop-in upgrade**: it opens the same `db.sqlite` and the same `/config`
+ `/data` volumes as before, so existing shares keep working. The browser-side
zero-knowledge crypto and the whole UI stay in TypeScript — only the server moved.

## Go backend (the big one)

- The Node/Next.js server is replaced by one CGO-free Go binary (`chi` + `tusd` +
  pure-Go `modernc.org/sqlite`), serving the existing React client as embedded
  static assets plus the JSON/file API. Result: a ~15 MB `distroless` image, much
  lower RAM, first-class HTTP streaming + Range, and no more native-addon build
  pain. No `docker run` change needed — same ports, env vars, and volumes.
- Drop-in compatibility: the SQLite schema is a byte-for-byte mirror of the old
  one and the blob layout is unchanged, so existing shares (and the previous DB)
  are served identically. The previous image is preserved at `Dockerfile.next`
  for rollback.
- Every auth gate is enforced server-side and constant-time (upload password,
  download key-verifier, manage token); a full adversarial security audit found
  no blocking issues. CI now builds + boots the image and runs the real
  zero-knowledge browser round-trip (upload → download → preview → multi-file)
  against the Go server on every change, plus `govulncheck` on the dependencies.

## Seekable encryption format (faster large-video preview)

- New per-file content format (`cf=2`): each 64 KiB chunk is encrypted
  independently with XChaCha20-Poly1305, so any chunk decrypts on its own. This
  gives **true random-access seeking** for large encrypted videos — the preview
  fetches and decrypts only the chunks it needs instead of from the start.
- Fully backward compatible: existing shares (the previous sequential format)
  keep working unchanged; new uploads use the seekable format automatically. Still
  zero-knowledge — the security core was reviewed independently.

## Video preview fix

- Inline preview of large videos (over the in-memory cap, streamed via the
  service worker) now works on the **first** visit to a share link, not only
  after a manual reload. Previously the streaming preview gave up before the
  service worker had taken control of the page, so no preview appeared.
- More formats offered for inline video preview — `.mkv`, `.avi`, `.mpeg`,
  `.3gp`, `.wmv`, `.flv`, `.ts` and more. Note a preview only PLAYS when the
  browser can decode the container's codec (mp4/webm/ogg/mov are reliable; avi/
  wmv/flv usually are not and show a safe, inert player).
- Faster to start: the streamed preview now serves a bounded window per request
  instead of fetching + decrypting the whole file up front, so playback begins
  quickly instead of hanging on a long initial load.

## UI polish

- **Home page** redesigned in a clean, Smash-style layout: no separate drop-zone
  box — the big, responsive, centered logo IS the upload target (click it to pick
  files, or drag files anywhere onto the page); the text moves to the top.
- **"Your link is ready" window** reorganized for a cleaner hierarchy (share link
  + QR), and the two copy buttons now share one consistent colour (they differed).
- **Bigger inline preview**: previewed images / videos / PDFs render at a proper
  viewing size instead of a small thumbnail, and the redundant icon inside the
  download card was removed (the brand header already carries it).
- **Consistent, centered windows**: the feather, the options panel, the result
  card and the download page all sit centered in the viewport. Choosing a file
  cross-fades the feather into the options panel (upload progress shown below it),
  and the copy-link button now has a clear hover state.
- **Removed the management/delete link.** Shares are removed purely by their
  expiry (and by the download limit, if set) — simpler, one less secret to keep.
  (Any management links already handed out stop working.)

## Branding

- New banner claim — "Big files, zero baggage." — and copy that positions
  featherdrop as your own private, self-hosted WeTransfer: no accounts, no size
  paywalls, links that self-destruct on schedule.

## Notes

- This bundles everything since v5.0.0 into one major. v5.0.0's features
  (multi-file shares, inline image/video/audio/text/PDF preview, optional upload
  password) are included; the early-delete management link from v5.0.0 has been
  removed — share removal is handled by expiry (and the optional download limit).
- Upgrade is drop-in. If you ever need to roll back, the previous Node image is
  still buildable from `Dockerfile.next`.
